content: 1. Rifapentine reduces the plasma concentration and therapeutic effect of vonoprazan by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 2. Vonoprazan decreases the plasma concentration and therapeutic effect of rilpivirine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This contraindication applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is not recommended. 3. Vonoprazan increases the plasma concentration and therapeutic effect of sirolimus by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely when these drugs are co-administered. 4. Vonoprazan is a weak inhibitor of CYP3A enzymes. Exercise caution when co-administering with drugs that are sensitive substrates of CYP3A. 5. Sotorasib reduces the plasma concentration and therapeutic effect of vonoprazan by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 6. St. John’s Wort reduces the plasma concentration and therapeutic effect of vonoprazan by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 7. Vonoprazan increases the plasma concentration and therapeutic effect of tacrolimus by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely when these drugs are co-administered. 8. Vonoprazan increases the plasma concentration and therapeutic effect of theophylline by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely when these drugs are co-administered. 9. Vonoprazan increases the plasma concentration and therapeutic effect of triazolam by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely when these drugs are co-administered. 10. Vonoprazan is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to any of its components, including amoxicillin or other beta-lactam antibacterials (e.g., penicillins, cephalosporins). 11. Co-administration of vonoprazan with lurasidone or rilpivirine-containing products is contraindicated due to inhibition of gastric pH by vonoprazan, which affects drug absorption. 12. Serious and occasionally fatal hypersensitivity reactions, such as anaphylaxis, anaphylactic shock, rash, erythema multiforme, and Henoch-Schönlein purpura, have been reported with vonoprazan or its components. Discontinue therapy immediately and initiate appropriate treatment if hypersensitivity occurs. 13. Acute tubulointerstitial nephritis (TIN) has been reported with vonoprazan. If TIN is suspected, discontinue therapy and evaluate the patient promptly. 14. Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SCAR), including Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), have been reported with all components of this drug combination. Additionally, drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) and acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis (AGEP) have been reported with amoxicillin. Discontinue therapy at the first signs of SCAR. 15. Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD) has been reported with acid-suppressing therapies and nearly all antibacterial agents. CDAD should be considered in all patients presenting with diarrhea following antibacterial use. A thorough medical history is necessary, as CDAD can occur over two months after administration of antibacterial agents. If CDAD is confirmed, discontinue the drug and implement appropriate management. 16. A high percentage of patients with mononucleosis who receive amoxicillin develop an erythematous skin rash. Avoid using amoxicillin in patients with mononucleosis. 17. Prescribing this regimen in the absence of a proven or strongly suspected bacterial infection or prophylactic indication is unlikely to provide benefit and increases the risk of drug-resistant bacteria. 18. Serum chromogranin A (CgA) levels may increase due to drug-induced decreases in gastric acidity. Elevated CgA levels can lead to false-positive results in diagnostic investigations for neuroendocrine tumors. Assess CgA levels at least 14 days after treatment and consider repeating the test if initial levels are high. 19. High urine concentrations of amoxicillin may cause false-positive results in glucose tests based on the Benedict copper reduction reaction. Use enzymatic glucose oxidase-based tests instead while taking amoxicillin. 20. Available pharmacovigilance data on vonoprazan use in pregnant women are insufficient to evaluate the drug-associated risk for major birth defects, miscarriage, or other adverse maternal or fetal outcomes. Report pregnancies to Phathom Pharmaceuticals, Inc., via their adverse event reporting line at 1-800-775-PHAT (7428). 21. Vonoprazan is generally considered safe for use during pregnancy, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. 22. Vonoprazan may be taken with or without food. 23. Store vonoprazan at 20–25°C (68–77°F), with brief exposure to 15–30°C (59–86°F) permitted. Protect the medication from light. 24.
